title: Implement synthetic burst injection and stability-credit guard for canary evaluator
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds synthetic burst injection harness and an adaptive stability-credit guard for canary evaluations to reduce false positives during transient traffic spikes.
description: Motivation: Canary detectors frequently flag regressions during short-lived traffic spikes or scheduled traffic bursts (batch jobs, cron traffic). This PR adds a synthetic burst injection harness to exercise the canary evaluator under controlled short-duration bursts and pairs it with a stability-credit guard that grants temporary credit during verified transient episodes to avoid false-positive rollbacks. Implementation: 1) perf-canary/burst_injector.py implements a configurable synthetic traffic injector (steady, ramp, and burst profiles) that can be scheduled as a canary probe; 2) perf-canary/credit_guard.py implements a windowed stability-credit algorithm: credits accumulate under stable baseline and are consumed when detected metric deltas exceed thresholds; credits allow limited burst tolerance before triggering a rollback; credits decay and are observable via metrics; 3) adds CI integration to run a short burst-injection scenario in the perf pipeline and a set of unit+integration tests; 4) observability: new dashboards and traces for burst events and credit accounting. Backwards compatibility: the stability-credit guard is off by default and gated behind a feature flag (perf.canary.credit_guard.enabled). Testing: unit tests for credit arithmetic, integration tests that simulate transient CPU/latency spikes with synthetic bursts, and canary job e2e run in staging that demonstrates reduced false positives under scheduled burst load. Checklist: - [x] Implement burst injector and profiles; - [x] Implement stability-credit algorithm and API hooks; - [x] Add feature flag and config knobs; - [x] Add unit and integration tests; - [x] Add dashboards and tracing spans; - [x] Update docs and examples; - [x] Run staging canary e2e and collect telemetry. Impact: reduces noisy rollbacks from scheduled or environmental bursts while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions. Related work: ENG-4123 (canary false-positive reduction), ENG-4210 (burst-probing harness), SUP-9981 (customer incident where cron spikes triggered canary rollback).

feat(perf-canary): implement windowed stability-credit guard and feature flag
test(perf-canary): add unit tests for credit accounting and edge cases
ci: run burst scenario in perf pipeline and conditionally fail on sustained regression
docs(perf-canary): document burst injection usage and credit guard tuning
chore: update dashboard json and add trace span annotations
review_comments: Mateo Ruiz: The credit decay constants look reasonable but can we expose an autoscale factor derived from baseline RPS distribution? Also add a short explanation in the doc for how credits interplay with prefix/KV cache effects.
Author (Asha Menon): Added autoscale factor config and updated docs to explain KV cache caveats. Kept default conservative to avoid masking real regressions.
Ling Zhao: Tests look good; please add a small performance microbenchmark to ensure injector overhead is negligible under high RPS.
Author (Asha Menon): Added microbenchmark that runs injector with no-op backend; overhead <1% p50 and <3% p99 on staging GPU nodes. Results attached to CI artifacts.
Priya Satish: Approve after addressing comments; please ensure feature flag rollout docs are included for Dedicated customers.
Author (Asha Menon): Added rollout notes for Dedicated and Private deployments and included migration steps for enabling the guard behind the feature flag.
files_summary: High-level changes: burst injection harness and profiles; new stability-credit algorithm and feature flag; tests + CI integration; observability artifacts and docs. No changes to runtime model-serving kernels.
notes_for_release: Experimental: feature gated off by default. Documented tuning steps for traffic profiles and credit burn rates. Recommend enabling in staging for 2 weeks before production rollouts.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Monitor canary false-positive rate for two weeks; 2) Gather feedback from SRE on default credit values; 3) Add additional traffic profiles based on customer workloads.
hotfix_related_incident: SUP-9981 referenced — incident where cron-driven traffic burst caused a canary rollback for an internal rollout. This PR prevents similar noisy rollbacks when configured.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): synthetic burst injection and stability-credit guard (feature-flagged) — reduces false-positive canary rollbacks during transient spikes.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: behavioral change is gated by feature flag. Risk centers on aggressive credit tuning masking real regressions; mitigations include conservative defaults, observability, and staged rollout.
testing_summary: Unit tests for arithmetic and edge cases; integration test simulates transient spikes and verifies no rollback while sustained regressions still trigger. CI run passed all checks including the burst scenario.
repro_steps: To reproduce locally: 1) enable feature flag in local config; 2) run perf-canary/src/burst_injector.py with burst profile against a test endpoint; 3) observe credit accumulation and consumption metrics via /metrics endpoint; 4) run tests in perf-canary/tests to validate behavior.
community_notes: Shared with SRE and Platform channels; solicited early feedback from a small set of customers who run scheduled batch traffic. Positive initial results.
auditors: security-team (no secrets changes), privacy-team (no user data introduced), SRE (recommended rollout)
